title: Pivot the column size of 50,000 and input file size is 17 TBs
question:
I have parquet files in aws s3 with size of 17 TBs with below schema and Unique Ids values are of size 50,000 :

UUID, Id

Which need to be transformed into below data structure(Basically Pivoting):

UUID, Id1, Id2, Id3,......

This output has to be written back into aws s3 in new path.

I tried with below approaches:

unique_ids = membership_df.select("Id").distinct().rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
#print(f"Number of unique IDs: {len(unique_ids)}")

pivoted_df = membership_df.groupBy("uuid").pivot("Id", unique_ids).agg(lit(1))
transformed_df = pivoted_df.fillna(0)

After running 10 hrs in databricks, failed because less space left on device, unable to initialize the HikariCP, connection time out etc. in different execution.

Used: r6id16xlarge 50 workers.

Can someone help me to get efficient way to transform this data please?
answer:
The above operations could be optimised using pair RDD. As records of the Pair RDD are colocated which will optimized your id collection.

I persisted the intermediate output to MEMORY and DISK, try first with r6id16xlarge with block storage of more than 60 TB if its insufficient try with higher instance.

Try following pyspark code:

from operator import add
from pyspark.storagelevel import StorageLevel

df_pairs_rdd = df.rdd.map(lambda x: (x['uuid'], x))
agg_keys_rdd = df_pairs_rdd.groupByKey().mapValues(lambda x: [y['id'] for y in x] )
agg_keys_rdd.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)

idkeys = agg_keys_rdd.flatMap(lambda x : x[1]).map(lambda x: (x,1)).reduceByKey(add)

allKeys = sorted(idkeys.keys().collect())
bkeys = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(allKeys)

present_keys_rdd = agg_keys_rdd.map(lambda k_v: id_present(k_v, bkeys))

cols = ['uuid'].__add__(allKeys)
output_df = present_keys_rdd.toDF(cols)
output_df.format("parquet").mode("overwrite").save("path")

Python Lambda Function for converting to RDD to DF column format.

from pyspark.sql import Row

def id_present(k_v, bkeys):
    bvIds = bkeys.value
    idset = k_v[1]
    presentlist = []
    for v in bvIds:
        if v in idset:
           presentlist.append(1)
        else:
           presentlist.append(0)

return Row(k_v[0], *presentlist)
